newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two new Russian fixed-rate bonds to trade Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Two new Russian fixed-rate bonds to trade Thursday.

text.p: Two new fixed-rate Russian bonds will start trading from Thursday, the Central Bank of Russia said.

The OFZ bonds, currently in the central bank's portfolio and not previously traded, are a two-year 2.90 trillion rouble issue, series number 25015, and a three-year 1.05 trillion rouble, series 25016, it said in a statement. Currently only one fixed-rate issue trades -- the 500 billion rouble 25001 bond maturing June 1999.

The authorities created fixed-rate bonds last year by converting central bank credits to the government into the new securities. But they were acquired by the national savings bank Sberbank and the central bank, and not freely traded. The first 20 percent series 25001 bond was released for trading in February this year.

The two bonds released on Thursday, which also pay an annual coupon of 20 percent, were restructured from another 11 bonds, series 25002 to 25012, created last year, but so far not traded openly. In March this year the authorities also created two 10 percent bonds, so far unpublicised -- series 25013 maturing in March 2001 and series 25014 maturing in March 2002, which remain in the central bank's portfolio, central bank sources said. These are the longest Russian securities so far issued.
Other OFZ bonds issued over the last few years have a floating rate linked to the yield on GKO discount Treasury bills maturing around the time coupons are paid.
